amc12-2003-12b-07.title: Eliminate nickels
amc12-2003-12b-07.body:
Let there be $n$ nickels, $d$ dimes, $q$ quarters: $n+d+q=100$ and $5n+10d+25q=835$. Dividing the second by $5$: $n+2d+5q=167$. Subtract the first: $d+4q=67$.

So $d=67-4q$, and $n=100-d-q=33+3q\ge0$ always. $d\ge0$ needs $q\le16$. Largest $d=67$ ($q=0$), smallest $d=3$ ($q=16$). Difference $64$.

**Answer: (D) 64**

amc12-2003-12b-09.title: Proportional differences
amc12-2003-12b-09.body:
For a linear function, differences in output are proportional to differences in input. Going from $2$ to $12$ is $\frac{10}{4}=2.5$ times as far as from $2$ to $6$, so the difference is $2.5\cdot12=30$.

**Answer: (D) 30**

amc12-2003-12b-10.title: Adjacent or not
amc12-2003-12b-10.body:
Two of the five sides of a regular pentagon are either adjacent or separated by one side. By the pentagon's rotational and reflection symmetry, all adjacent pairs give congruent figures, and all non-adjacent pairs do too. The two types are not congruent. So $2$ figures.

**Answer: (B) 2**

amc12-2003-12b-10.title: Count pairs
amc12-2003-12b-10.body:
There are $\binom52=10$ pairs of sides: $5$ adjacent and $5$ non-adjacent. Rotations of the pentagon carry any adjacent pair to any other, and the same for non-adjacent pairs. An adjacent pair makes two triangles share a vertex of the pentagon, a non-adjacent pair doesn't, so the two kinds differ. $2$ figures.

**Answer: (B) 2**

amc12-2003-12b-11.title: Rate of the watch
amc12-2003-12b-11.body:
In $60$ real minutes the watch advances $57.6$ minutes, i.e. $0.96$ of real time. For the watch to show $10$ hours $=600$ minutes after noon, the real time elapsed is $\frac{600}{0.96}=625$ minutes $=10$ h $25$ min. Actual time: 10:25 PM.

**Answer: (C) 10:25 PM**

amc12-2003-12b-11.title: Proportion in seconds
amc12-2003-12b-11.body:
Watch: $3456$ s per real $3600$ s, ratio $\frac{24}{25}$. Watch time $10$ h corresponds to real time $10\cdot\frac{25}{24}$ h $=10\frac{5}{12}$ h $=10$ h $25$ min.

**Answer: (C) 10:25 PM**

amc12-2003-12b-17.title: Linear system in the logs
amc12-2003-12b-17.body:
Let $u=\log x$, $v=\log y$: $u+3v=1$ and $2u+v=1$. Solving: $u=\frac25$, $v=\frac15$. So $\log(xy)=u+v=\frac35$.

**Answer: (D) $\frac35$**

amc12-2003-12b-17.title: Combine the equations
amc12-2003-12b-17.body:
Both logs equal $1$, so $xy^3=x^2y$, giving $x=y^2$. Then $\log(xy^3)=\log(y^5)=5\log y=1$, so $\log y=\frac15$ and $\log(xy)=\log(y^3)=\frac35$.

**Answer: (D) $\frac35$**

amc12-2003-12b-18.title: Match exponents
amc12-2003-12b-18.body:
For the minimum, $x$ should only contain the primes $7$ and $11$: $x=7^m11^n$. Then $7x^5=7^{5m+1}11^{5n}$ must equal $11\cdot y^{13}$, so $y$ is also built from $7$ and $11$, and we need $13\mid 5m+1$ and $13\mid 5n-1$.

Smallest: $5m+1=26$, $m=5$; $5n-1=39$, $n=8$. So $x=7^5\,11^8$ and $a+b+c+d=7+11+5+8=31$.

**Answer: (B) 31**

amc12-2003-12b-18.title: Verify
amc12-2003-12b-18.body:
With $x=7^5 11^8$: $7x^5=7^{26}11^{40}$ and $11y^{13}$ with $y=7^2 11^3$ gives $11\cdot7^{26}11^{39}=7^{26}11^{40}$ ✓. Smaller exponents fail: $5m+1\equiv0\pmod{13}$ has smallest solution $m=5$, and $5n\equiv1\pmod{13}$ has smallest $n=8$.

**Answer: (B) 31**

amc12-2003-12b-19.title: Count
amc12-2003-12b-19.body:
$|S|=5!-4!=96$. With second term $2$ and first term not $1$: the first term is $3$, $4$ or $5$, and the other three terms can be arranged in $3!=6$ ways: $18$ permutations. Probability $\frac{18}{96}=\frac3{16}$, so $a+b=19$.

**Answer: (E) 19**

amc12-2003-12b-19.title: Conditional probability
amc12-2003-12b-19.body:
Given the first term is not $1$, it is $2,3,4,5$ equally likely. The second term is $2$ requires the first term $\ne2$ (probability $\frac34$), and then $2$ is one of the $4$ remaining numbers for position $2$ (probability $\frac14$): $\frac34\cdot\frac14=\frac3{16}$. $3+16=19$.

**Answer: (E) 19**

amc12-2003-12b-20.title: Use the roots at ±1
amc12-2003-12b-20.body:
From the graph, $f(1)=0$, $f(-1)=0$ and $f(0)=2$. So $d=2$, and
$a+b+c+d=0$, $-a+b-c+d=0$. Adding: $2b+2d=0$, so $b=-d=-2$.

**Answer: (B) $-2$**

amc12-2003-12b-20.title: Factor
amc12-2003-12b-20.body:
Since $\pm1$ are roots, $f(x)=(x^2-1)(ax+k)=ax^3+kx^2-ax-k$. Then $f(0)=-k=2$, so $k=-2$, and $b=k=-2$.

**Answer: (B) $-2$**

amc12-2003-12b-21.title: Law of cosines
amc12-2003-12b-21.body:
The interior angle at $B$ is $\pi-\alpha$, so $AC^2=64+25-80\cos(\pi-\alpha)=89+80\cos\alpha$. $AC<7$ means $89+80\cos\alpha<49$, i.e. $\cos\alpha<-\frac12$, i.e. $\alpha>\frac{2\pi}{3}$. Probability $\frac{\pi/3}{\pi}=\frac13$.

**Answer: (D) $\frac13$**

amc12-2003-12b-21.title: The critical triangle
amc12-2003-12b-21.body:
When $AC=7$, the triangle with sides $8,5,7$ has angle at $B$ given by $\cos B=\frac{64+25-49}{80}=\frac12$, so $B=60^\circ$. $AC$ grows with the angle at $B$, so $AC<7$ exactly when the angle at $B$ is below $60^\circ$, i.e. the turn $\alpha$ exceeds $120^\circ$. Probability $\frac{60^\circ}{180^\circ}=\frac13$.

**Answer: (D) $\frac13$**

amc12-2003-12b-22.title: PQ is a diagonal of a rectangle
amc12-2003-12b-22.body:
Let $O$ be the center. The diagonals are perpendicular, so $OPNQ$ is a rectangle and $PQ=ON$. The minimum of $ON$ for $N$ on $AB$ is the distance from $O$ to line $AB$. In right triangle $AOB$ with legs $8$ and $15$ and hypotenuse $17$, that distance is $\frac{8\cdot15}{17}=\frac{120}{17}\approx7.06$.

**Answer: (C) 7**

amc12-2003-12b-22.title: Coordinates
amc12-2003-12b-22.body:
Put $O$ at the origin, $A=(-8,0)$, $B=(0,15)$. A point on $AB$ is $N=(-8+8t,15t)$; then $P=(-8+8t,0)$, $Q=(0,15t)$, so $PQ^2=(8-8t)^2+(15t)^2$. Minimizing: derivative $-128(1-t)+450t=0$ gives $t=\frac{64}{289}$, and $PQ^2=\frac{14400}{289}$, $PQ=\frac{120}{17}\approx7.06$.

**Answer: (C) 7**

amc12-2003-12b-23.title: Estimate
amc12-2003-12b-23.body:
The count is about $\frac{10000-1000}{\pi}=\frac{9000}{\pi}\approx2865$. That's closest to $2900$.

**Answer: (A) 2900**

amc12-2003-12b-24.title: Compare slopes
amc12-2003-12b-24.body:
$y=|x-a|+|x-b|+|x-c|$ is piecewise linear with slopes $-3,-1,1,3$ on the intervals separated by $a,b,c$. The line $y=2003-2x$ has slope $-2$.

For $x<a$, the graph falls faster than the line; for $x>a$ the graph falls slower or rises. So the difference (graph minus line) decreases until $x=a$ and increases afterwards. Exactly one solution means the minimum of the difference is $0$, i.e. the line passes through the corner $(a,\,(b-a)+(c-a))$:
$$2003-2a=b+c-2a\implies b+c=2003.$$
With $b<c$, the smallest $c$ is $1002$ (with $b=1001$, and any $a<1001$).

**Answer: (C) 1002**

amc12-2003-12b-24.title: Check with numbers
amc12-2003-12b-24.body:
Take $a=1$, $b=1001$, $c=1002$. At $x=1$: $y=0+1000+1001=2001=2003-2\cdot1$ ✓. To the left of $x=1$, the absolute-value graph rises by $3$ per unit leftward while the line rises by only $2$, so no more intersections; to the right, the graph has slope $\ge-1>-2$, so it stays above the line. If $c\le1001$, then $b+c\le2001<2003$, so at $x=a$ the line is above the graph; the line then crosses the graph once on each side of $a$, giving two solutions. So $c=1002$ is minimal.

**Answer: (C) 1002**

amc12-2003-12b-25.title: Angles
amc12-2003-12b-25.body:
A chord is shorter than the radius exactly when its central angle is less than $60^\circ$. Fix the first point at angle $0$ and let the others be at angles $\theta_1,\theta_2$, uniform in $(-180^\circ,180^\circ)$.

All three pairwise angles below $60^\circ$ requires $|\theta_1|<60^\circ$, $|\theta_2|<60^\circ$ and $|\theta_1-\theta_2|<60^\circ$. In units of $60^\circ$ this is the square $(-1,1)^2$ (area $4$) minus two corner triangles of area $\frac12$ each: area $3$. The whole sample space has area $6^2=36$. Probability $\frac3{36}=\frac1{12}$.

**Answer: (D) $\frac1{12}$**

amc12-2003-12b-25.title: Leftmost point
amc12-2003-12b-25.body:
All three points lie within an arc of $60^\circ$. Exactly one of them comes first going counterclockwise through that arc. For a given point $X$ to be first, the other two must land in the $60^\circ$ arc counterclockwise from $X$: probability $\left(\frac16\right)^2=\frac1{36}$. These $3$ events are disjoint, so the probability is $\frac3{36}=\frac1{12}$.

**Answer: (D) $\frac1{12}$**
